facts.text: The node reads the odom_id parameter with the default absolute name /odom and advertises a nav_msgs::Odometry publisher on it.

publishOdom converts agent 0's map pose into the odom frame with transformPose and returns false without publishing when transformPose fails; otherwise it publishes the pose with frame odom, child frame base_link and agent 0's linearVelocity and angularVelocity.
transformPose returns false when the tf listener's transformPose throws.
main constructs the node with a public handle n and the private handle pn('~').
The node sleeps 0.5 s and then uses sfm::MAP.
MAP is defined as RosMap::getInstance(), which returns a function-local static RosMap.
The RosMap constructor calls the static_map service once and stops with ROS_FATAL and ROS_BREAK when the call fails.
After simulator::run the loop sets agent 0's linearVelocity and angularVelocity to the simulator's selectedLinVel and selectedAngVel.
The node opens metrics.txt and writes its header line.
Once a second the loop appends each agent's velocity and nearest-person and nearest-obstacle distances to metrics.txt.
The node reads the scan360_id parameter with the default absolute name /scan360 and advertises a sensor_msgs::LaserScan publisher on it.
The scan geometry is built from the configured reading count, robot radius and maximum scan range: the angular limits are -M_PI and M_PI and the increment is 2*M_PI/scan360_readings.
The scan loop ray-casts from the robot pose, treats an intersecting person as scan_range_max, and clamps every reported range to at least robot_radius and at most scan_range_max.
The node reads its parameters through pn and advertises six publishers; it registers no subscriber, service server or action server in this block.
The main loop broadcasts the map-to-odom transform, calls publishOdom and publishScan360 on every iteration and sleeps on a ros::Rate built from freq until the node handle shuts down.
The launch file starts map_server with maps/temple.yaml, the enps_dwa_node executable and RViz.

The README states that the software simulates human agents and a dual-wheeled non-holonomic robot, that the simulation runs until the user kills the process, and that the ENPS model selects motion commands with DWA.
The README documents ROS Noetic, compilation with catkin_make and starting the example with roslaunch enps_dwa temple.launch.

determinism.notes: The fake returns fixed placeholder samples per subscription; it runs no social-force or ENPS/DWA step and does not reproduce a trajectory or state hash.

fidelity.engine: analytic: ROS-free transport fake (no physics, no planner)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free transport fake: it answers the declared subscribe operations with placeholder messages and runs no simulation loop, social-force model, ENPS membrane model, DWA selection, map ray-casting or physics

the fake's scan has eight placeholder ranges; the upstream default scan360_readings is 1440 and is overridable, so the deployed array length follows the operator's configuration and is not a fixed contract of this package

the upstream /odom publication depends on a map-to-odom transform; the fake always answers a fresh subscription and does not reproduce the transform-failure path except through its documented negative switches

the package exposes only the /odom and /scan360 observations; the upstream /people, /detections, /trajectories and /forces MarkerArray topics, TF broadcasts, metrics.txt output and all private ROS parameters are NOT COVERED

the upstream node advances its own world at the freq parameter rate (default 30 Hz); there is no environment-step, velocity-command, pause or reset endpoint in the pinned clone, so the driver cannot step or reset the simulation
review: an MHS e-stop is a software latch only; the node keeps running, its robot keeps driving under the planner and its pedestrians keep walking until the process is killed

review: at start-up the node calls map_server's static_map service once, 0.5 s after it starts, and stops with ROS_BREAK when the call fails, so if map_server (started by the same launch file) is not yet serving, /odom and /scan360 never appear; /odom also stays silent until the node's tf listener has its own map-to-odom broadcast
review: the node writes metrics.txt into its working directory and the shipped launch file also starts RViz; neither is part of this package's contract

measures.description: Subscribe to one fresh nav_msgs/Odometry sample on the simulator's /odom topic and return the robot pose, twist, header frame and stamp. No motion is commanded.
measures.name: read_odometry

measures.description: Subscribe to one fresh sensor_msgs/LaserScan sample on the simulator's /scan360 topic and return the message under scan, including its header, scan geometry, range limits and ranges. No motion is commanded.
measures.name: read_laser_scan

safe_state.description: No native stop exists: the MHS latch only refuses this package's own reads, while the simulator keeps advancing at its freq rate with its robot driving under the ENPS/DWA planner and its pedestrians walking until the node is killed; this package commands no motion.
